{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-wv-class-e","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"e78968952ff1d26b2ed00151db08e69af5b42869991f47731c98f2970c1441b5","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-wv-class-e:lineage:33","source_registry_sha256":"2261abaab8e2b1aaff5b8a336e3bfcf845adaa75847f0210442061783d7f9afb","source_liveness_sha256":"9a1fb68777f5e9d5c4b27899084cc233b265410fee506dfe6554447a61ea026e"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Signals and markings","heading":"C — Signals and markings","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Signals and markings

FACT_ID: sec08-F01 | anchor: A01
Railroad crossing signs may be round or diamond-shaped and yellow with black symbols, or black letters on white bars in the shape of an X called a crossbuck, and a sign below the crossbuck gives the number of tracks when there are two or more [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F02 | anchor: A01
Some railroad crossings have electrical devices such as bells, flashers and automatic gates to signal an approaching train, you must yield to all trains, and failing to stop when the lights are flashing or a barrier is down results in a citation [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F03 | anchor: A01
Where there are two or more tracks you must be alert for a second train on the other set of tracks, and you should not enter a crossing until the vehicle ahead has moved far enough that you can clear the tracks, or you may be trapped and hit by another vehicle or a train [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F04 | anchor: A01
A driver facing a circular green signal may enter the intersection and go straight, turn right or turn left unless signs or pavement markings prohibit a movement, every turn follows the right-of-way rules, and a left turn on circular green must yield to oncoming vehicles [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F05 | anchor: A01
A green arrow, shown alone or with other indications, lets drivers enter the intersection to make the movement the arrow shows, and a green arrow in a left-turn signal usually means that opposing traffic is stopped [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F06 | anchor: A01
A steady circular yellow means the green is ending and will change to red, you should drive through a yellow only if your vehicle is already within the intersection clearance, and a yellow arrow means the green arrow is ending and will change to red [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F07 | anchor: A01
Traffic facing a steady circular red must stop unless making a movement permitted by a green arrow, and must remain stopped until another indication allows it to proceed, the only exception being a permitted turn on red [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F08 | anchor: A01
A driver may turn right on red at the intersection of two-way streets, or turn left on red from a one-way street onto another one-way street, but only after yielding to all other traffic and pedestrians and only where no sign prohibits the turn [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F09 | anchor: A01
A steady red arrow requires a complete stop before the intersection, stop line or crosswalk for the direction the arrow shows, and the driver must remain stopped as long as the arrow is red [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F10 | anchor: A02
At certain intersections flashers supplement or replace stop signs, showing circular flashing red in all directions or circular flashing yellow for the through traffic [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F11 | anchor: A02
A driver facing a circular flashing yellow may proceed through the intersection with caution, while a circular flashing red is the same as a stop sign and requires a complete stop and yielding to all other traffic and pedestrians [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F12 | anchor: A02
When traffic control signals are not needed or are out of order they may be placed in flashing operation, and they then work the same as intersection flashers [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F13 | anchor: A02
Lane use control signals show a green downward arrow when traffic may use the lane under it, a yellow X when the lane is about to close or reverse direction and you should move out as soon as you can, and a red X when the lane is closed or carrying opposing traffic and must not be used [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F14 | anchor: A02
Special lane signals are used where the direction of a street or of certain lanes changes during the day, and they indicate how each lane may be used [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F15 | anchor: A02
Crosswalk signals are traffic signals for pedestrians who must obey them, a hand symbol or the words don't walk means pedestrians are not to cross, and a walking figure or the word walk means they may cross inside the crosswalk lines [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F16 | anchor: A02
Crosswalks at intersections and in school zones signal a high pedestrian traffic zone, and being especially alert for pedestrians there reduces the risk of crashes [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F17 | anchor: A02
A blind person on foot who uses a guide dog or other service animal or carries a white cane or walking stick has the right-of-way on any highway, street or road whether or not in a crosswalk [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F18 | anchor: A03
Pavement markings warn, regulate and inform traffic like highway signs, white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction, and yellow lines separate lanes moving in opposite directions [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-F19 | anchor: A03
Broken yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions, and when the broken yellow line is on your side of the road you may pass when it is safe [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-F20 | anchor: A03
Solid yellow lines also separate opposing traffic, a solid yellow line on your side of the road means you must not pass, and on interstates, one-way streets and divided four-lane roads a solid yellow line marks the left edge of the pavement [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-F21 | anchor: A03
On roadways with more than one lane moving in the same direction the lanes are separated by broken white lines, sometimes with broken black lines added for visibility, and you drive within the lines and never straddle them except when changing lanes [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-F22 | anchor: A03
Solid white lines mark the edge of the pavement and help you stay on the road at night or in bad weather, and where solid white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction you do not change lanes [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-F23 | anchor: A03
White diamond shapes painted in a lane tell drivers the lane is designated for car pools, bicycles or buses [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-F24 | anchor: A03
Center left-turn lanes are reserved for left turns from either direction and are never through or passing lanes, and you recognize them by the solid yellow lines nearest the through lanes with broken yellow lines to the left of them [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-F25 | anchor: A03
Reversible lanes, used where traffic is heavy at certain times of day, are marked on both sides by a double broken yellow line, and this is the only case in which a driver may drive for any distance to the left of a yellow line [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-F26 | anchor: A03
Many crosswalks are marked by solid white lines running all the way across the pavement at intersections and sometimes between them, some crosswalks especially in residential areas are unmarked, and you must not block a crosswalk with your car [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-F27 | anchor: A03
Stop lines are wide white lines painted across the traffic lanes to mark where you must stop at an intersection, keeping you clear of pedestrians and cross traffic, and where there is no stop line or crosswalk you stop before entering the intersection where you can see traffic from all directions [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]
